Title: Policies for information security
How it is met / justification: Security policy statement for the service: scope; rules for access; data; change and incidents; reviewed quarterly

Title: Information security roles and responsibilities
How it is met / justification: One operator holds every role (owner; administrator; incident handler; data controller); stated in the pack

Title: Segregation of duties
How it is met / justification: Single operator; no duties can be separated. Compensating control: a branch ruleset lets a change reach main only through a pull request that passes CI

Title: Management responsibilities
How it is met / justification: The operator owns the pack and the residual risks and reviews both quarterly

Title: Contact with authorities
How it is met / justification: Contacts documented for incident reporting: BSI/CERT-Bund; the Berlin data protection authority; Oracle abuse desk

Title: Contact with special interest groups
How it is met / justification: No community sharing yet
Gap / action: Share honeypot indicators with a community feed such as AbuseIPDB

Title: Threat intelligence
How it is met / justification: The honeypot itself produces threat intelligence: every event is mapped to a MITRE ATT&CK technique and published live

Title: Information security in project management
How it is met / justification: Threat model and risk assessment written before deployment; security requirements tested

Title: Inventory of information and other associated assets
How it is met / justification: Asset inventory with owner and classification for every asset

Title: Acceptable use of information and other associated assets
How it is met / justification: Rules for honeypot data: research and public statistics only; no re-identification; no sharing of raw logs

Title: Return of assets
How it is met / justification: No employees or contractors hold assets of the service

Title: Classification of information
How it is met / justification: Three classes (Public; Internal; Confidential) applied in the asset inventory

Title: Labelling of information
How it is met / justification: Classification follows storage location (public repo and pages are Public; VM raw logs and the SSH key are Confidential); no labels on individual files

Title: Information transfer
How it is met / justification: All transfer is encrypted: HTTPS for the API and pages; SSH for administration; the API is read-only and cross-origin access is limited to the demo site

Title: Access control
How it is met / justification: Administration only by SSH key on a separate port; the public API exposes only read-only; masked data; no write endpoints

Title: Identity management
How it is met / justification: One named admin account on the VM (key-based); root login disabled; one GitHub account owns the repositories

Title: Authentication information
How it is met / justification: SSH passwords disabled; admin key is ed25519
Gap / action: The admin private key has no passphrase: add one

Title: Access rights
How it is met / justification: Only the operator has access to the VM and repositories; access reviewed quarterly with the evidence snapshot

Title: Information security in supplier relationships
How it is met / justification: Supplier register with the risk each supplier brings and how it is handled

Title: Addressing information security within supplier agreements
How it is met / justification: Standard terms of Oracle Cloud and GitHub apply; both offer data processing agreements
Gap / action: Record which DPA version applies to each account

Title: Managing information security in the ICT supply chain
How it is met / justification: Honeypot software pinned to exact versions; datasets verified by SHA-256; Dependabot proposes updates for pip; Docker and Actions

Title: Monitoring, review and change management of supplier services
How it is met / justification: An uptime check watches GitHub Pages and the VM every 30 minutes; a supplier change (LinkedIn flagging sslip.io) was handled as incident INC-07

Title: Information security for use of cloud services
How it is met / justification: Oracle Cloud Always Free VM in the EU (Frankfurt); provider controls inherited
Gap / action: Upgrade to Pay As You Go so Oracle cannot reclaim the idle VM; set a 1 EUR budget alert

Title: Information security incident management planning and preparation
How it is met / justification: Incident response playbook with severity levels; roles and contacts

Title: Assessment and decision on information security events
How it is met / justification: Triage rules separate expected honeypot attacks (events) from incidents that affect the service

Title: Response to information security incidents
How it is met / justification: Eight real incidents recorded with response; root cause and fix

Title: Learning from information security incidents
How it is met / justification: Every incident ends with a lesson and where possible a regression test

Title: Collection of evidence
How it is met / justification: Read-only evidence script collects the VM's security configuration; snapshots are committed

Title: Information security during disruption
How it is met / justification: If the VM fails the demo pages and console keep working and the tracker shows Tracker offline; no security control depends on the VM being up

Title: ICT readiness for business continuity
How it is met / justification: The VM can be rebuilt from the repository with two commands; recovery time objective 1 hour
Gap / action: Run and time a rebuild drill once a year

Title: Legal, statutory, regulatory and contractual requirements
How it is met / justification: GDPR record of processing and legitimate-interest assessment; EU AI Act classification; NIS2 scope check

Title: Intellectual property rights
How it is met / justification: Code under the MIT licence; datasets and the DB-IP database credited under their licences

Title: Protection of records
How it is met / justification: Results; risk register and evidence snapshots are versioned in git

Title: Privacy and protection of PII
How it is met / justification: Addresses truncated and counted with a daily-keyed hash; passwords never stored by the tracker; tracker data kept 30 days; raw honeypot logs 7 days

Title: Independent review of information security
How it is met / justification: No independent review yet
Gap / action: Ask a qualified peer to review the pack and the VM once a year

Title: Compliance with policies, rules and standards for information security
How it is met / justification: A test checks that every evidence file named in this SoA exists; the VM evidence is re-collected quarterly

Title: Documented operating procedures
How it is met / justification: Deployment; rebuild and evidence collection are documented and scripted

Title: Screening
How it is met / justification: No staff are employed

Title: Terms and conditions of employment
How it is met / justification: No staff are employed

Title: Information security awareness, education and training
How it is met / justification: The operator holds an MSc in Cybersecurity and CompTIA Security+

Title: Disciplinary process
How it is met / justification: No staff are employed

Title: Responsibilities after termination or change of employment
How it is met / justification: No staff are employed

Title: Confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements
How it is met / justification: No third party has access to confidential information of the service

Title: Remote working
How it is met / justification: All administration is remote over key-based SSH from the operator's laptop (see 8.1)

Title: Information security event reporting
How it is met / justification: The public reports vulnerabilities through GitHub private reporting; the uptime check emails the operator

Title: Physical security perimeters
How it is met / justification: VM in Oracle's Frankfurt data centre and pages on GitHub; physical security is the providers' (both ISO/IEC 27001 certified)

Title: Physical entry
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Securing offices, rooms and facilities
How it is met / justification: The service has no office

Title: Physical security monitoring
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Protecting against physical and environmental threats
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Working in secure areas
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Clear desk and clear screen
How it is met / justification: Applies to the operator's laptop
Gap / action: Confirm automatic screen lock on the operator's laptop and record it

Title: Equipment siting and protection
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Security of assets off-premises
How it is met / justification: The operator's laptop holds the admin key
Gap / action: Confirm disk encryption on the operator's laptop and record it

Title: Storage media
How it is met / justification: No removable media are used for the service

Title: Supporting utilities
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Cabling security
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Equipment maintenance
How it is met / justification: Provider data centre controls

Title: Secure disposal or re-use of equipment
How it is met / justification: Cloud storage is sanitised by the provider when released

Title: User endpoint devices
How it is met / justification: The operator's laptop is the only endpoint with admin access
Gap / action: Confirm disk encryption; screen lock and automatic updates; add a passphrase to the SSH key

Title: Privileged access rights
How it is met / justification: Root login disabled; sudo only for the key-authenticated admin; containers drop all Linux capabilities and add back only what each needs

Title: Information access restriction
How it is met / justification: The API returns only masked fields and never the address hash; raw logs are readable by root only

Title: Access to source code
How it is met / justification: Public read access by design; only the operator can write; main cannot be deleted or force-pushed; GitHub secret scanning and push protection are on

Title: Secure authentication
How it is met / justification: SSH: key only; passwords and keyboard-interactive login disabled
Gap / action: Confirm two-factor authentication on the GitHub and Oracle accounts

Title: Capacity management
How it is met / justification: Memory limits per container; swap on the 1 GB VM; limits on API batch size; page size and live viewers

Title: Protection against malware
How it is met / justification: Low-interaction honeypot: attackers get no shell and uploads are never executed; containers are read-only
Gap / action: No malware scanner on the VM: accepted while no files are stored

Title: Management of technical vulnerabilities
How it is met / justification: Automatic security updates on the VM; Dependabot alerts; security updates and monthly grouped updates; every update is built and smoke-tested (including the honeypot images) before it merges; pinned container images

Title: Configuration management
How it is met / justification: All configuration is in git and deployed from it; container hardening is part of the configuration

Title: Information deletion
How it is met / justification: Tracker events deleted after 30 days; raw honeypot logs rotated daily and kept 7 days

Title: Data masking
How it is met / justification: IPv4 shown without the last octet; IPv6 as its /48; distinct sources counted with an HMAC whose key changes daily and is never stored

Title: Data leakage prevention
How it is met / justification: The API cannot return raw addresses; passwords or hashes; secret scanning blocks pushed credentials
Gap / action: No leakage monitoring on the VM: accepted for its data

Title: Information backup
How it is met / justification: Code; configuration and evidence are in git on GitHub and on the operator's laptop
Gap / action: Tracker data is not backed up: accepted (30-day statistics that refill within hours)

Title: Redundancy of information processing facilities
How it is met / justification: Demo pages and the console run on GitHub Pages independently of the VM
Gap / action: Single honeypot VM: accepted for a demonstration service

Title: Logging
How it is met / justification: Every honeypot event is logged and processed into the tracker; web server and collector log to the container runtime

Title: Monitoring activities
How it is met / justification: Uptime check every 30 minutes alerts if pages fail or no attack has been logged for 3 hours

Title: Clock synchronization
How it is met / justification: VM clock synchronised by NTP; all events stored in UTC

Title: Use of privileged utility programs
How it is met / justification: No admin utilities are exposed; containers run without a shell for attackers and with no extra privileges

Title: Installation of software on operational systems
How it is met / justification: Software reaches the VM only through apt and container images built from the repository

Title: Networks security
How it is met / justification: Host firewall allows only the fake services; HTTPS and the admin port; everything else is rejected

Title: Security of network services
How it is met / justification: HTTPS with HSTS; a strict content security policy; cross-origin access limited to the demo site

Title: Segregation of networks
How it is met / justification: The collector API listens on localhost only and is reached through the web server; the admin port is separate
Gap / action: Containers share the host network so the honeypot sees real source addresses: accepted

Title: Web filtering
How it is met / justification: No users browse the web from the service

Title: Use of cryptography
How it is met / justification: TLS certificates from Let's Encrypt; SSH ed25519 keys; HMAC-SHA256 with daily keys for counting sources

Title: Secure development life cycle
How it is met / justification: Threat model first; tests and container smoke test on every push

Title: Application security requirements
How it is met / justification: All attacker-supplied text is treated as hostile: cleaned; length-capped and escaped; API input validated

Title: Secure system architecture and engineering principles
How it is met / justification: Least privilege; read-only containers; collection separated from presentation; defence in depth (host firewall plus cloud security list)

Title: Secure coding
How it is met / justification: Parameterised SQL; output escaping; no inline script; tests for hostile input

Title: Security testing in development and acceptance
How it is met / justification: Hostile-input tests; smoke tests of the service and the honeypot containers; ONNX parity test; adversarial evasion test of the model

Title: Outsourced development
How it is met / justification: No development is contracted out; third-party components are covered by 5.21

Title: Separation of development, test and production environments
How it is met / justification: Development on the laptop; tests in CI; production on the VM
Gap / action: No staging VM: changes go from CI to production

Title: Change management
How it is met / justification: Every change reaches main through a pull request that must pass the CI test check (GitHub branch ruleset); then it is deployed and the evidence snapshot re-collected

Title: Test information
How it is met / justification: Tests use synthetic data and public datasets; no attacker data from the VM is used in tests

Title: Protection of information systems during audit testing
How it is met / justification: Evidence collection is read-only and prints no secrets or log contents
